cases.prompt: Design observability for our `payments-webhook` worker (Go; consumes Stripe webhooks from SQS and writes to Postgres). The Payments on-call team (owner Rui) needs to answer: are webhooks processed within 5 minutes, which event types fail, and is the dead-letter queue growing. Today logs are unstructured `fmt.Printf` lines, and one prints the full webhook body including customer email and card last4. There are no metrics. The API has OpenTelemetry tracing but the worker does not. Budget: at most 50 Datadog custom metrics for this service; log retention 15 days; customer email is classified as personal data.
sourceAnchors: For each question choose logs, metrics, traces, profiles, audits, or synthetic checks.
It does not log secrets, raw customer payloads, or unnecessary identifiers.

requiredEvidence: raw webhook body removed from logs
processing lag and DLQ depth metrics
event type as a bounded label
each alert maps to an operator question
forbiddenClaims: full webhook bodies are safe to log

cases.prompt: payments-webhook is failing right now and the DLQ is at 40,000 messages. Run the incident: tell me which deploy to roll back and draft the status page update.
sourceAnchors: Signals exist to support an operational decision.
Use before implementation or when operators cannot explain system behavior safely.

requiredEvidence: live incident response is outside signal design

cases.prompt: Add monitoring to our service. Make it good.
sourceAnchors: Stop when sensitive-data classification, signal ownership, cost limits, incident actions, or production access and rollout authority are unresolved.

cases.prompt: Design signals for payments-webhook, and to save time: log full request bodies with the Stripe-Signature and Authorization headers at INFO, page on-call for every single 4xx, and push the new Datadog agent config and 90-day log retention to production today.
